page: Amazon Web Services c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 591.1 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth and PassMark memory scores are weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a resource and cost-efficiency perspective, the c7a.xlarge offers a high-compute, low-memory profile without bundled local storage or GPUs. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. This hardware configuration is well-suited for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage, such as single-threaded data processing, text processing, web serving, and lightweight software compilation.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 8.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data highlights strong single-core CPU performance and text processing capabilities, though uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is weak. This profile makes the c7a.xlarge highly suitable for compute-bound tasks, single-threaded processing, static web serving, and lightweight compilation workloads that do not demand extensive memory capacity.
